sites.name: Williston Highway 1804 / 48th Street NW
sites.load: No viable scope established; historic 30 MW crypto proposal denied
sites.owner: Multiple tax owners; offered schedule unconfirmed
sites.summary: The advertised group spans different tax owners. County records tie the eastern 76-acre parcel to a 2024 data-center setback denial; no current lawful cure or subject MW allocation was found.

sites.next_test: Ask the broker for the exact current lot/APN schedule and the county for any written decision curing the February 2024 denial on 35-035. Hold paid pursuit absent that evidence.

blocks.text: The material changes

Williston is materially weaker than its morning listing-only rank: the county denied a setback appeal tied to the exact eastern 76-acre parcel in February 2024. New Castle has a more favorable soil screen, but the matched tax geometry intersects two utility territories. Rooks has inconsistent marketing versions for acreage, building plans and power. Dillon still needs its exact supplier and RU use path.

Hinds 110 remains the existing global founder focus. This four-site work order does not replace that decision or reopen other sites. All four remain research cases, with no validated buyer, no verified available MW and no paid-control clearance.

Deal IDs: Rooks oct19-38995811; Dillon sc-dillon-53; New Castle oct19-27254380; Williston oct19-3934635. Private internal screening. Public records are dated evidence, not title, engineering or utility commitments.

pages.title: Compare research effort, not imaginary capacity.

blocks.text: What the business might be: identify land where a buyer could lawfully build a data center, resolve the hard questions cheaply, then transfer useful rights and evidence with appropriate professional advice. A buyer pays only if that work saves more time or money than its own land search or another campus. No such premium is established here.

Suggested next-hour allocation

Give Rooks and New Castle the next documentary work blocks. Continue Dillon’s existing utility / planning / layout questions. blocks.text: Resolve the broker-version conflict first

The Showcase-linked 74-acre brochure advertises a 10 MW substation in process for Q1 2027. The six-page brochure linked directly on CBRE’s 36-acre listing does not make that MW/date statement and uses a different warehouse plan. No file date proves which commercial scope supersedes the other. Request the controlling plan and APS writing; do not carry the number into available MW. [AZ1–AZ4]
What can make it worthwhile

A buyer-accepted 5–10 MW first phase with dry or low-water heat rejection could use less land and power than the earlier 25 MW working screen. Local observation is inexpensive. A credible seller-cooperation or buyer-funded diligence arrangement would be more plausible than assuming cheap control of multimillion-dollar industrial land. Those are hypotheses, not accepted terms.
What can stop it

No parcel-specific APS commitment; an unaffordable price or exclusivity premium; data-center or accessory-use conflict; water / fire-flow limits; adjacent residential noise constraints; flood / drainage / easement issues; no buyer-compatible diverse fiber. No evidence yet establishes a net contiguous buildable pad or assignment value.

pages.title: Rooks: make a visit answer specific questions.

blocks.text: Visit from public roads, or enter only with owner/broker permission. Match the north parcel and expansion boundary to the broker’s survey. Photograph access points, gates, drainage channels / culverts, overhead corridors and visible construction with date, location and viewing direction. Record nearby homes and noise sources. Ask which photographed substation is meant by the marketing claim.

Before a dedicated trip, request the current 36-acre price and APS documents. Bring the APN map and note whether frontage / access shown in marketing exists on the ground. A photograph cannot establish a legal access right, reserved MW, carrier diversity or flood status. Keep observations separate from agency or utility determinations.

NWI returned no features in the queried two-parcel envelope. Flood clearance was not obtained: the Assessor Flood service’s queried layer returned a null-geometry county object, unsuitable for a flood-zone intersection. Buckeye planning services required a token, so exact-use interpretation remains a written city question. [AZ4, AZ6, AZ9, G1]

blocks.text: The live AFM 53 listing still shows 60 acres and $696,000. A fresh county response matches Baker Anne A, deed 492/54 and plat 18/1. The public zoning-point response is RU Rural. These establish a traceable tax parcel and current marketing; they do not establish seller signing authority, legal access or data-center permission. [SC1–SC4]
The physical concern persists

The approximately 60-acre polygon is long and narrow. Fresh NWI intersection is about 1.13 acres of mapped riverine features. The Oct 8 dominant-soil screen carried forward roughly 25.13 acres somewhat poorly drained and 3.85 acres poorly drained; roughly 48% combined. The 48 challenger had more well-drained mapped soil but about 3.53 mapped NWI acres. These are overlapping screens, not additive exclusions or net pad areas. [G1, G2; Oct 8 Dillon baseline]
Power and demand remain the first commercial tests

Public electric overlays do not resolve the exact retail supplier. The nearby Carolinas I-95 Super Park’s Duke / cooperative, voltage and utility descriptions apply to that park, not Baker land. Its documented industrial offering is also a substitute that a buyer can evaluate. Syncranicity needs a specific advantage over that alternative, not a proximity narrative. [SC5]

Next: one combined 53/48 document request for surveys, access/easements, existing utility studies and a written county RU-use path. Proceed only with unpaid research; the current power, layout and buyer proof is too weak for an option.

pages.title: Dillon: mapped water is only part of the test.

blocks.text: What changed in the policy watch

SC PSC docket 2026-138-E is an open generic large-load proceeding, with workshops listed for October 26–27, 2026. It does not supply an adopted price or a Baker load commitment. H.5286 is a proposed state moratorium bill; the reviewed status did not show enactment. Neither should be transformed into an automatic parcel approval or an active statewide ban. [SC6, SC7]

Current FEMA NFHL retrieval returned 503. Earlier county flood tiles were only a visual proxy. The resulting flood gate stays unresolved. Do not label the roughly 58.9 acres outside mapped NWI as buildable: setbacks, drainage, easements, flood, access and an actual low-water campus layout still need a combined constraints test.

Written county question: for 080-00-00-053 and 048, identify the controlling jurisdiction and adopted RU use classification for a 20–25 MW non-crypto data center, plus generators, batteries, electrical yard and cooling. State approvals, setbacks, noise limits, appeal timing and any current prohibition. The City of Dillon code must not be substituted for county rules. [SC3, SC4]

rows: The 30 MW GoGo proposal on exact parcel 35-035 failed one-mile sensitive-property and three-mile existing-data-center separation tests. Staff would not accept the CUP application; switching cooling did not cure the identified issue.
Appeal denied 5–0. This is stronger negative evidence than a generic political-risk proxy.
Signed data-center ordinance remains listed. No written subject cure was found. The historical denial is not called a permanent ban.

blocks.text: The ordinance regulates a broader data-center use, not merely cryptocurrency. Quiet HPC cannot be assumed exempt. Requirements include CUP review, acoustic work, a signed electric power agreement and maintenance / reclamation security. A current county interpretation is the responsible next source. [ND3–ND6]
Do not confuse the later GoGo approval

A later LU-0073-24 packet concerns a proposed 10-acre site in Section 12, T153N R103W, Hardscrabble Township. It includes an up-to-8 MW interruptible MWEC arrangement. The screened parcel is Section 35, T154N R102W, Judson Township. The later case demonstrates the sort of specific issuer evidence needed; it supplies no permit or power right here. [ND7]

pages.title: Williston: separate the owners, land and power rights.

blocks.text: The two western Yellowstone parcels report 15.0146 and 51.6692 county GIS acres; their combined approximately 66.7 acres match the scale of a separately marketed 67-acre sibling site. This is an identity clue, not a confirmed offered schedule. Do not assign the eastern denial to every western acre, or assume the western offering escapes the same ordinance. [ND1, ND2]

The current broker brochure contains an unfilled MW placeholder. No subject service agreement was recovered. MWEC’s published C4 tariff is a benchmark, not a total delivered-cost quote. The Basin public onboarding one-pager shows funded studies and a $50,000 nonrefundable application stage, with multiyear implementation phases. Confirm the current version and applicability with MWEC; the newer link was behind member login. [ND8, ND9]

That published application fee alone is five times the founder’s $10,000 cumulative all-in soft-control cap. If applicable, a credible sponsor must fund it; shrinking the land lot does not prove an exemption. Oil / pipeline / terminal neighbors also warrant a buyer-specific hazard and Phase I path. NWI returned no features in the covered 76-acre envelope; flood, soil/geotechnical and environmental clearance remain open.

U = required proof unresolved. H = capital/runway hold. A = adverse exact-parcel history requiring current cure. Desktop tax and GIS evidence improves the file but does not satisfy the complete proof at its required scope.

No complete PASS is asserted. Several proof components have authoritative public evidence; the remaining private, professional or scope-specific pieces are material. No available-MW, COD, buyer commitment, assignable control, usable-acre or profit value is invented.

Policy precedence: founder-approved September 8, 2026 policy v2 requires all 16 proofs, conservative score at least 70 and evidence confidence at least 85 before founder review of paid control. Even a passed review authorizes no money automatically. Existing $5,000 learning and $10,000 cumulative all-in soft-control limits for one paid parcel remain controlling.

A complete 52-factor register and 34-topic coverage register are in the JSON. Unresearched components remain NOT_REVIEWED or UNKNOWN. This memo is a targeted desktop screen, not a completed 116-question pre-option clearance. An independent professional red team has not reviewed it.

blocks.text: Worst-loss rule: count nonrefundable premiums, counsel, reports, deposits, extension payments and nonrecoverable travel once, as cumulative exposure. Downside can be the entire funded amount with no assignment. Purchase money, infrastructure, tariffs, deposits, taxes and construction remain unpriced. No assignment premium, profit margin, ROI or takeout probability is established.
Cheapest proposed structure to discuss, only after evidence improves

Request existing documents and permission for nonintrusive investigation first. An owner-authorized access / information agreement may support early desktop or professional scoping without an option. If control becomes justified, seek a conditional, assignable or nominee-compatible instrument, objective diligence exits, fixed price, defined utility milestones, reliance / sharing rights and affordable extension rights. Local counsel must resolve authority, access, licensing / compensation and transaction triggers.

Draft seller language: “I am evaluating a defined data-center use and will not represent the land as powered. Would you provide the current survey, title and utility file, permit limited investigation, and discuss conditional control only after the issuer evidence supports the scope?” No terms were proposed or accepted in this run.

Stop if the legal use has no documented cure; seller refuses useful access / assignment; essential offsite rights are unavailable; load / carrier timing outruns affordable control; required studies or security lack sponsor funding; or a buyer would choose a better substitute. No paid vendors commissioned. Obtain scoped civil, environmental and local counsel quotes only after the next decisive free documents support proceeding.

blocks.text: Transferable evidence plan

Keep each offered survey / legal description with its own APNs; store issuer letters with scope/date and sharing terms; separate marketing from capacity. A buyer room should contain the current source ledger, contradictions, parcel map, utility / carrier / planning responses, capital exposure and unresolved questions. Share third-party material only with appropriate rights; do not promise reliance the issuer has not granted.
What this pass corrected

A ranked listing is not a qualified site. Williston’s later approval belonged to a different township and parcel. New Castle’s listing pin was unsuitable for constraints. Rooks’ directly linked brochure differed from the 74-acre power-marketed version. Dillon’s industrial-neighbor utility facts did not transfer to Baker land. These distinctions should persist in the Deal Desk.

Learning assignment: read the Basin large-load onboarding one-pager [ND8]. Ask: who is the actual applicant, which money is nonrefundable, and can funded rights / studies transfer to the intended buyer? Then apply the same questions to APS, REMC/Duke and Dillon’s eventual supplier.

Checked October 19, 2026 unless a historical date is shown. V1 = marketing/proxy; V2 = attributable context; V3 = authoritative public record at its stated scope; V0 = failed or unusable retrieval. No V4 subject utility, title, carrier or professional commitment was recovered.
